title: Assemble a voice-matching email prompt
scenario: A client was charged for a fourth storage week after their goods had already shipped — a billing mistake on your side. You need a reply that apologizes, explains the fix, and does not promise compensation you are not authorized to give.
task: Fill every field to assemble a prompt for a reply email that sounds like you — then compare with a strong example.

fields.label: Outcome — what the email must achieve
fields.placeholder: Apologize plainly, explain the refund, give the next step…

fields.label: Voice — two emails you actually sent
fields.placeholder: Paste one or two short emails you have written…

fields.label: Facts and boundaries — what must be in it, what must not be promised
fields.placeholder: Include the fourth-week refund; no discounts or future credits…

fields.label: Guard — placeholders instead of invented details
fields.placeholder: Use [refund reference] style placeholders for anything I must fill in…

sampleSolution:
Write a reply email to a client who was billed for a fourth storage week after their goods had already shipped — our mistake.

The email must: apologize plainly, state that the fourth week will be refunded, and give a clear next step with a date.

Match the voice of these two emails I have sent before:
[paste example 1]
[paste example 2]

Do not promise anything beyond the refund — no discounts, no future credits, no service-level commitments.

Where a detail is not in my notes, insert a bracket placeholder like [refund reference] for me to fill in before sending.

Context:
[paste the facts of the case]
hints: Adjectives like 'friendly' cannot be checked; examples can.
What convention keeps the model from inventing an amount, a date or a reference?
explanation: Two examples replace a page of tone adjectives, and the boundaries line fences off the promises you cannot make. The placeholder rule leaves visible gaps — [refund reference] — instead of plausible inventions you might send by accident. A draft you must complete is exactly the right shape for consequential email.
